walkthroughs.body_html:
Shakespearean tragedy traces a noble protagonist's catastrophic descent. Hamartia (a tragic flaw) and external pressure converge.

The final scene often restores order — Fortinbras's arrival in Hamlet, Malcolm's coronation in Macbeth.

Comedies move through misrule (disguises, crossed lovers) into restoration. Most end with multiple weddings — the marriage plot enacts social healing.

The 'green world' (Northrop Frye) — forests and islands — is the comic stage of transformation.
The history plays dramatise dynastic struggle for Tudor audiences. They blur genres — Henry IV mixes tragic kingship with Falstaff's comic excess.
